key_insight: A multi-protein serum/CSF signature can stratify survival in ALS better than clinical variables and neurofilament light chain alone.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this protein panel could help enrich ALS trials and improve prognostic conversations by giving a more precise estimate of disease progression.
method: High-depth proximity extension assay proteomics on 1,095 serum/CSF samples from 426 people with ALS.
Age- and sex-adjusted Cox models to find proteins associated with survival.
Penalised Cox regression and external cohort replication to build and test a 9-protein serum panel.
evidence_signal: The study analyzed 1,095 samples from 426 ALS patients and replicated findings in an independent cohort of 349 patients, with 57 serum and 5 CSF proteins linked to survival at FDR-adjusted p<0.05.
watch_item: This is a biomarker study, so prospective validation and real-world standardization are still needed before the signature can be used clinically.
paper_title: A proteomic signature for prognostic stratification in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
